about.text: 🚀 The greatest satisfaction comes from the process of turning an idea into a real project – an application, a website, or content that reaches an audience and delivers tangible results. I value the ability to create solutions from scratch and bring them to a point where they generate business value, reach, or engagement. Every project is an opportunity to combine technology, strategy, and creativity into practical results.
about.text2: 💻 I combine backend and frontend to deliver comprehensive solutions – from intuitive interfaces to efficient systems behind the scenes. I create web applications, websites, and process automations, focusing on functionality, usability, and business value. This allows me to take a project from an idea all the way to a finished product.
about.text3: 🎬 Creating content became a natural complement to my work in IT. I develop projects in video, marketing, and visual communication, using editing tools and strategies that engage audiences. I combine technical knowledge with a creative approach, producing promotional videos, marketing materials, and other types of content that support brands and businesses.
about.text4: 💡 Every project should bring real value. A website – supports business goals, an application – solves specific problems, automation – saves time and resources. I focus on analyzing needs and delivering solutions tailored to users and organizations. For me, growth, efficiency, and quality matter.
about.text5: Outside of IT and marketing projects, I spend a lot of my free time on my own ideas. Currently, I’m tinkering with my own application, experimenting with features and solutions that could make it stand out. I have an idea for a computer game and want to test my skills in game development, and I plan to eventually release it. I combine my passion for games with my technical and creative skills, hoping to create something truly exciting.

hosting.q: Will you take care of hosting?
hosting.a: Yes. I'll help you choose hosting for the project and set it up. A simple site can often be hosted very cheaply, while an app with a backend needs a server — I'll recommend the most sensible option.

domain.a: If you already have a domain, I'll connect it to the new site. If not, I'll help you choose and register one in your name, so it always belongs to you.

content.q: Who prepares the copy and photos?
content.a: We settle this in the first call: you can provide ready materials, I can prepare them, or we work with someone else. Graphics and photos are handled the same way.

time.a: It depends on the scope: a landing page or business card site usually takes a few weeks, an application longer. I give you a specific deadline together with the design and quote.

time.a: It depends on the format: a reel or an episode edit usually takes a few days, a full promo video from one to several weeks. We agree on the deadline up front, and when footage arrives last minute I do my best to deliver on time without cutting corners.

revisions.a: We agree on the number of revision rounds together with the quote. Small changes after the presentation are made right away — I want you to be fully happy with the result.

formats.q: What file format will I get?
formats.a: By default MP4 (H.264) at the resolution and aspect ratio of the target platform: 16:9 for YouTube and websites, 9:16 for reels. Graphics come as PNG or JPG. Other formats on request.

recording.a: Either option works. For promo videos I do the filming. For vlogs and gaming you usually record, and I take the raw footage and handle the editing.

aureliahr.summary: A team management web app built as my engineering thesis.
aureliahr.problem: Information about a team, its tasks and responsibilities is often scattered across spreadsheets, emails and chat apps — it's hard to get one up-to-date picture of the team's work.
aureliahr.solution: I designed and built a React web app backed by MongoDB that brings team data and work together in one place.
aureliahr.result: A working application delivered as my engineering thesis — the full stack from interface to database. The code is available on GitHub.

gpsmaker.summary: A Python and pandas script that processes CSV files with GPS data.
gpsmaker.problem: Cleaning up large CSV files with GPS points by hand is tedious and error-prone.
gpsmaker.solution: I wrote a Python script that uses pandas to load, clean and transform GPS data into the required format.
gpsmaker.result: Repeatable data processing with a single script run instead of manual spreadsheet work.

webscraping.summary: My first script that ended up being used by others.
webscraping.problem: The data we needed was only available on web pages — copying it by hand took a lot of time.
webscraping.solution: I wrote a Python script that automatically fetches and saves the data from those pages.
webscraping.result: Other people started using the tool — my first code with real users.

noescapecursor.summary: A program that locks the cursor to the primary monitor while a selected game or app is active.
noescapecursor.problem: On multi-monitor setups the cursor in fullscreen games can slip onto another screen and minimise the window at the worst possible moment.
noescapecursor.solution: I built a lightweight program that detects the selected game or app and locks the edges of the primary monitor while it runs.
noescapecursor.result: The cursor stays where it should, and the program runs in the background with no extra setup.

portfolio.summary: This website — a bilingual showcase combining a client offer with a profile for recruiters.
portfolio.problem: The previous version mixed roles and styles, had no offer or path for recruiters, and the code was full of duplication.
portfolio.solution: I rebuilt the site with React, TypeScript and Tailwind: a UI component system, data in typed modules, PL/EN translations, service pages and a portfolio with case studies.
portfolio.result: A consistent, accessible and fast site on GitHub Pages that's easy to extend — a new project is a single data entry.

feedback.text1: Full professionalism, but with a relaxed vibe – just the way I like it. The website works great, looks awesome, and the whole process was stress-free. Highly recommend!
feedback.text2: I had the opportunity to work with Jacek several times over the past year and watched with appreciation how much effort he puts into learning and how much progress he has made. He went from creating a simple Python script that generates PDFs from HTML to building a full application in React with a Django backend. He’s able to find solutions on his own, learns quickly, and isn’t afraid of challenges. As an IT team leader, I’m convinced that with this mindset, he will quickly become a valuable member of any team.
feedback.text3: Working with Jacek was absolutely smooth and professional from start to finish. The website he created for me exceeded my expectations – it's modern, clear, responsive, and perfectly reflects the character of my brand. I was especially impressed by his personalized approach, quick communication, and great understanding of my needs. Every adjustment was implemented instantly, and the entire process went efficiently and in a friendly atmosphere. I wholeheartedly recommend working with Jacek Kozłowski to anyone looking for a reliable and creative web designer. It’s an investment that truly pays off!
feedback.text4: Awesome collaboration! The concept, execution, and attitude were 100%. Thanks for handling everything – I didn’t have to worry about a thing.
feedback.text5: Ambitious and highly dedicated, which is clearly reflected in the projects he completes. I'm very satisfied with the results and will definitely come back again. Highly recommended! 😊

footer.tagline: Developer & Video Creator. I build websites, apps and video content that work for your business.

career.headline: Full-stack developer (React · Python/Django) who blends code with video creation

summary.p1: I build web applications end to end — day to day I work with React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS, and on the server side with Python (Django, Flask) plus SQL and MongoDB databases. I completed the Web Front-end, Python Back-end and Full Stack Python Developer courses, and my engineering thesis was AureliaHR, a team management app.
summary.p2: My Python scripts were deployed at the company I work for — one of them cut a recurring task from 4–5 days down to two clicks. I also shoot and edit video, so I understand product and marketing, not just code. I run most projects on my own: from understanding the problem, through the docs, to deployment.

company_job.a1: Wrote a Python (pandas) script that processes CSV files with company-car GPS data — a task that took 4–5 days now takes two clicks.
company_job.a2: Built a web scraping script (BeautifulSoup) to analyse competitors' listings on external websites.
company_job.a3: Both tools were deployed and are used in the team's daily work.

freelance.a1: I design and build websites and web apps for small businesses — from a Figma mockup to deployment.
freelance.a2: I shoot and edit ads, reels and social media content.
freelance.a3: I handle client communication, quotes and project schedules on my own.

engineer.note: Engineering thesis: AureliaHR — a team management application (React, MongoDB).

courses.degree: Web Front-end Developer, Python Back-end Developer and Full Stack Python Developer courses
courses.note: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Python, Flask, Django, SQL and NoSQL databases, Git, Figma, Unix.

frontend.title: Frontend
frontend.text: I completed React courses covering React Router, React Query, Tailwind CSS and TypeScript, among others. I build projects — small and large — on my own, which taught me to find answers in documentation and adapt solutions to the project's needs. I use Tailwind in all my projects and know both its strengths and its limits.
frontend.highlight_text: The app helps companies manage teams and reduces communication chaos: employees talk within their own team, and managers handle contact between teams. Managers assign tasks and track their team's progress.

backend.title: Backend
backend.text: I started out self-taught, and after mastering the basics I completed the Python Back-end Developer and Full Stack Python Developer courses. There I learned the Flask and Django frameworks as well as working with Git, databases and Unix.
backend.highlight_title: In practice: scripts deployed at work
backend.highlight_text: I independently wrote two scripts used at the company: scraping competitors' listings (BeautifulSoup) and processing company-car GPS data (pandas), which cut the work from 4–5 days to two clicks.

databases.title: Databases
databases.text: At university and during the Full Stack course I worked with relational (SQL) and document (MongoDB) databases. I know when to choose which and how to design data structures with application performance in mind.
databases.highlight_text: The app stores user data and the tasks assigned to each team in MongoDB.

tools.title: Tools / DevOps
tools.text: I use Git every day — in my own projects and in team projects at university. I work with branches, keep commits and pull requests readable, resolve conflicts and take part in code reviews.
tools.highlight_text: I use GitHub and GitLab along with basic CI/CD features to automate testing and deployment. This website is published on GitHub Pages.

video.title: Video and graphics
video.text: I combine creative work with analytical thinking — editing and programming. That lets me care about both aesthetics and functionality when building websites and apps.
video.highlight_text: As an editor I learned timing, choosing music, writing copy and using AI to streamline work. I know the principles of scripting, shot planning, lighting, framing, color grading and composition.

dev_creative.title: I combine development with creativity
dev_creative.text: I code and edit video, so I look at a product through the eyes of users and marketing — not just through the code.

independence.title: I work independently
independence.text: I take most projects from zero to deployment. I look for answers in the docs instead of waiting for ready-made solutions.

shipped.text: Python scripts I wrote are used every day — one of them cut a task from 4–5 days to two clicks.
